definition: The electric force between two point charges is proportional to the product of the charges and inversely proportional to the square of their separation, $F = k\frac{q_1 q_2}{r^{2}}$, where $k = \frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}$ in a vacuum; like charges repel and unlike charges attract.
The total electric charge of an isolated system stays constant: charge can move from one body to another but is never created or destroyed.
The fact that the charge on any free particle or body is a whole-number multiple of the elementary charge, $q = ne$, so charge changes only in steps of $e$.
The size of the charge on a proton or an electron, $e = 1.60 \times 10^{-19}\ \text{C}$: the smallest charge found on any free particle.

An experiment in which charged oil drops were held still between horizontal charged plates, so that the electric force balanced their weight; every charge measured was a whole-number multiple of $e$, which is evidence that charge is quantised.

The separation of charge in a conductor caused by a nearby charged body, without contact: charge opposite to the body's gathers on the near side and like charge on the far side, while the conductor's total charge is unchanged.
Connecting a conductor to the Earth (grounding), so that electrons can flow between the conductor and the Earth; the Earth is so large that its own charge does not change noticeably.
